title: A Finite Polylogarithm Alphabet for Rational Hankel Sums
review_status: Research draft; not externally peer reviewed or proof-assistant formalized.
priority_scope: New contributions are compared only with the inspected ProveIt sources; no exhaustive historical-priority claim.

claims.statement: Confluent pole factorization and the optimized formal harmonic-weight bound W_r, including the positive-marginal formula.

A terminating exact compiler for rational Hankel cutoff generating functions with poles at nonpositive integers, using rational combinations of positive-index multiple polylogarithms of weight at most W_r.
All ranks with reduced denominator degree at most two lie in the rational span of 1, -log(1-z), log(1-z)^2, and Li_2(z), with arbitrary polynomial part.
Single-pole formal sharpness and an explicit Gamma-product formula for a highest-weight harmonic coefficient. This is not a minimal polylogarithm-weight theorem.
Several-simple-pole highest harmonic coefficient, fixed-size Christoffel/Hahn compression, and generalized-eigenvalue description of one-residue exceptions.
Necessary and sufficient finite jet tests for endpoint principal-part cancellation; explicit three-pole example with a double endpoint pole.
Spectral determinant generating identity and convergent multiple-zeta endpoint identities, including arbitrary spectral derivatives.
All-order ordinary convergent Stieltjes-difference and logarithmic-harmonic determinant identities obtained from the spectral family.
Two explicit harmonic-determinant Euler evaluations and a shifted-double-pole dilogarithm generating function; classical Euler-sum reductions are credited.
